root_cause.text: The function `bio_integrity_prep` in `block/bio-integrity-auto.c` only zeroes the integrity buffer for writes when protection information checksum type is `BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE`, missing the case where PI is generated but the metadata size exceeds the PI tuple size, leaving the opaque portion uninitialized.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "This misses the case where PI is generated and the PI tuple size is nonzero, but the metadata size is larger than the PI tuple. In this case, the remainder ("opaque") of the metadata is left uninitialized." The patch changes the condition from `bi->csum_type == BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE` to `bi->metadata_size > bi->pi_tuple_size`, ensuring zeroing whenever metadata is larger than PI tuple.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the zeroing condition to cover all cases where metadata size exceeds PI tuple size, not just when checksum type is none.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition in an else-if branch from checking if checksum type is 'BLK_INTEGRITY_CSUM_NONE' to checking if 'metadata_size' is greater than 'pi_tuple_size'.
intent_record.how: Now, instead of only setting the __GFP_ZERO flag when the checksum type is none, it sets the flag whenever the metadata size exceeds the pi tuple size, ensuring that the extra bytes beyond the PI tuple are zeroed during allocation.
